File a complaint if a player violates the Xbox Live Code of Conduct. If the player has not violated the Code of Conduct, consider submitting a player review instead.

All complaints are reviewed by Xbox Live. However, Xbox Live policy does not permit disclosure of the status or results of individual complaints.

Complaints do not affect matchmaking or the player's reputation.  Consider submitting a player review also if you want to avoid this player in the future.

What is Rep?
Your rep is your reputation on Xbox Live. It is a snapshot of how other players see you. Rep is determined by player reviews submitted about you. A high rep means other players like to play with you, and a low rep means many players want to avoid you. Your rep changes as other players submit player reviews about you. You can see your recent avoided player reviews on your gamercard.

Player Reviews:
When you avoid a player, you become less likely to be matched with that person in the future. This may also affect that player's rep. When you prefer a player, you become more likely to be matched with that person in the future. This may also affect that player's rep. You can change your review of a player by submitting a different review. Changing your review will not affect the player's rep.

Player reviews should be used for preference only and not for Code of Conduct violations. If a player violates the Code of Conduct, consider filing a complaint.

Your gamerscore is the sum of your achievements in all the Xbox 360 games you play. In a game, each achievement has a score. By unlocking achievements, you increase your gamerscore. Your achievement scores add up to the gamerscore displayed on your gamer card.

Xbox Live Gamer Zones are used for player matchmaking. Your choice of gamer zone will determine which game sessions you are most likely to join. Player matchmaking will help you find sessions with other players from the same gamer zone.

For example, if you select the Pro zone, you are most likely to play with other Pro zone players. If there are no suitable sessions in your zone, you can still play with players from other zones.
